A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research, with LoCAL renamed SV-RAG and LoCAL-Bench renamed VisR-Bench. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original retrieval, document-QA, efficiency and layer-ablation results in Tables 1–4 and Figure 4, plus qualitative results in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds retrieval comparisons, parser-based QA comparisons and timing results, including Tables F.1 and G.1.

M1.justification: Despite the rename and redrawn architecture, Section 3, Algorithm 1 and Equations 1–2 retain the same late-interaction retrieval, hardest-negative contrastive loss, shared backbone and separate retrieval/QA LoRA adapters. No procedural change is established.

E1.justification: Training sources and evaluation datasets remain the same. VisR-Bench is the renamed 226-document, 471-QA LoCAL-Bench. DocMatix-IR and PFL-DocVQA already appeared in v1; the new appendix experiments evaluate retained document-QA coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 expands retrieval comparisons beyond CLIP, BM25 and SBERT to SigLip, BGE-M3, BGE-large and NV-Embed-v2. Appendix G additionally evaluates Phi-3 and GPT-4o with parsed-text evidence and GPT-4o with retrieved images, substantially broadening the comparison methods.

E3.justification: Section 5.3 changes stated text extraction from PaddleOCR to a document parser for MMLongBench-Doc and VisR-Bench. Appendix G introduces GPT-4o-based binary answer judging through Mean GPT Score and text/image comparisons using retrieved versus all pages. Appendix F adds per-page timing comparisons. The original splits and main training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix E adds two text-only failure cases, Section 5.1 newly reports the approximately 1% MMLongBench retrieval effect of expanded training data, and Appendix G examines evidence modality and retrieval versus full context. The existing layer ablation and SlideVQA failure analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The new Mean GPT Score and aggregate results do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds baseline results and revises CLIP, BM25 and Col-Phi scores. MMLongBench BM25 top-1 changes from 5.2 to 25.3 alongside revised preprocessing; Col-Phi top-1 on the renamed benchmark changes from 66.9 to 71.9, changing the leading retriever. Tables F.1 and G.1 add timing and QA outcomes, including previously unreported VisR-Bench QA scores. Tables 2–4 remain numerically unchanged.

T1.justification: The retrieval definitions, contrastive-loss equation, training algorithm and Appendix B PNLS derivation are unchanged. The new GPT-based evaluation metric adds no formal theorem, proof or mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central efficiency, dual-adapter and performance claims. Section 7 narrows the novelty assertion from the first model performing retrieval and QA simultaneously to single-model visual retrieval-augmented generation specifically for document QA.

C2.justification: Appendix G adds explanations that broader textual context can support answers without images and that retrieving only evidence pages can hurt text-only VisR-Bench QA by removing useful context. These qualify retrieval's benefits; the existing fine-tuning, memory and untested-device limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 newly discloses GPT-4o filtering of duplicate images and unsuitable questions, retrieval-model variants, and dataset licensing, screening and source-link distribution policies. These disclosures do not establish changed training procedures. Conversely, the source-code availability footnote and URL disappear, along with the earlier SBERT/BM25 text-aggregation details.

R1.justification: v2 adds MM-GEM and distinguishes its natural-image similarity/caption training from document-focused dual adapters. It also adds a TextMonkey token-resampling comparison and references for LLaVAR and the new retrieval baselines. The broader related-work organization and positioning remain intact.

P1.justification: The method and benchmark are renamed, LMM terminology is largely changed to MLLM, and the title, author details and conference header are updated. An ethics statement and Appendices E–G are added, with localized prose revisions; most existing paragraphs and the main section sequence are preserved.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is extensively redrawn to expose shared layers and adapters, and Figure 1 explicitly shows the shared model and separate LoRA roles. Table 1 is expanded and regrouped, while Figures E.1–E.2 and Tables F.1 and G.1 add substantial new displays. Existing benchmark-distribution, layer-ablation and earlier appendix figures are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens support for the existing approach through more competitive retrieval baselines, direct parser-based QA comparisons, VisR-Bench QA results and retrieval timing evidence. Appendix G also clarifies when retrieval helps or loses useful context. These are useful, focused improvements to an already substantial evaluation. The removal of the source-code link is a reproducibility regression, and the new GPT-based scoring lacks an exact judging prompt, limiting the overall gain.
